headline: Chainflip reported theft of 122.86 BTC in addition to an Ethereum outflow estimated at $4.86 million, and Cyber warned users to avoid its bridge after unexpected token minting. Customers shared an OpenRouter warning of possible exposure of prompts sent to MiniMax, and Airbyte restored most functions after its Cloud security incident.

incidents.what: Chainflip confirmed that Bitcoin was stolen in addition to ether and stablecoins, and offered a bounty for returning the funds.
Microsoft said a server-side flaw let an unauthorized party read administrator email addresses and tenant metadata, with no unauthorized configuration changes found.
CNN, AP and Fox News independently cited sources describing an apparent intrusion into the FBI’s national crime database; the FBI declined to comment to AP.
Cyber confirmed unexpected token minting on Solana and an outflow from its Ethereum bridge reserve, and told users to avoid the bridge and exchange deposits.
incidents.scale: About 5.21M CYBER moved; final loss unknown

incidents.what: OpenRouter warned customers that some prompts sent to MiniMax may have been read and removed the affected endpoints’ zero-retention label.
Optimizely shut down a legacy deployment server and removed an injected script from two sites after finding unauthorized access.
Illinois disclosed an apparent intrusion attempt at the Algonquin Dam on the Fox River and said the dam continued to operate.
Airbyte restored Intercom after taking Cloud services offline for containment, but 15 other API connectors remained down.
French reports described an unverified claim involving student and tutor data, including contact and bank-account details.
Travelsoft began restoring the bookings platform in phases after shutting it down following unauthorized access.
The Icelandic provider’s managing director said seven websites were destroyed in the attack and that services would return in phases.
